summary: Tested the batching-technique extension to Purchasing Plan / MRP background BOM cache refresh (bom_cache_service.bulk_prefetch/_fetch_live_batch, purchasing_plan._resolve_boms, mrp_service.build_mrp_plan). Code review of bom_cache_service.py, purchasing_plan.py, mrp_service.py confirms the described behavior matches implementation exactly (_apply_override extraction, _fetch_live_batch chunking via BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE, bulk_prefetch idempotent pre-warm, refresh_stale_nodes batched). Live curl verification: cold Purchasing Plan run (target_month 2026-09) completed in 223s with EXACTLY 889 components / 7 missing_boms (matches main agent's claim); warm re-run completed in 172s with IDENTICAL 889/7 results and ZERO bom_cache_service warnings in backend log during either run (confirms cache-hit correctness). MRP generate via curl: 1466 components / 12 unresolved_items, locked_plan_id 6a77d716f299e46685acaebd - exact match to main agent's claim. UI verification (Playwright): Purchasing Plan page generates 889/7 correctly with no console errors; Missing BOMs table + 'Save & Retry' Fix Mapping flow tested on a not_found part (CLAMP 003A) - retried without crash, stayed 'Confirmed no BOM' as expected (SAP genuinely has no BOM for it); Production Planning tabs all regression-clean: Open PO Demand (786 lines) loads, BOM Alternates shows exactly 192 (matches iteration_67 baseline), MRP Plan tab renders the restored/regenerated 1466-component plan with 568 shortages and the 12-item unresolved banner, no console errors on any tab. Ran existing tests/test_bom_cache.py regression suite twice (once parallel via pytest.ini's baked-in -n auto, once as a targeted subset): TestBomCachePurchasingPlan.test_run1_cold_then_run2_warm_identical_and_faster and TestBomCacheStats both PASS consistently; test_run3_stable_after_cache_warm FAILS consistently (elapsed 59-61s vs hard-coded <20s expectation) - root-caused via backend log correlation to sap_valuation_client connect-timeouts on the SAP tenant's MaterialValuationDataValuationPriceCollection OData endpoint during that exact window, NOT to any bom_cache_service warning/failure - this is the same 'sap_valuation_client.py... independently slow this session' caveat the main agent explicitly flagged as out-of-scope/pre-existing, not a regression from this round's batching change. Also independently observed the same refresh_stale_nodes ~partial-failure pattern (many 'Background refresh: fetch failed for X, keeping existing cache entry' warnings) the main agent already disclosed and asked not to be flagged as blocking unless proven to be a construction bug - did not find evidence of a construction bug (no XML/parsing error observed, only ConnectTimeoutError to the SAP host itself).

minor.issue: Hard-coded 'elapsed3 < 20s' assertion fails (actual 59-61s) - root cause is sap_valuation_client connect-timeouts against the SAP tenant (unrelated pre-existing slowness this session, confirmed via backend log correlation), not the reviewed bom_cache batching code. Test assertion may need loosening if this SAP-side valuation slowness persists in future sessions.

action_items: No code fix required for this round's batching extension - correctness confirmed (identical 889/7 purchasing plan results cold vs warm, identical 1466/12 MRP results, zero bom_cache warnings during cache-hit runs).

Optional: consider loosening test_bom_cache.py's test_run3 <20s threshold or asserting on absence-of-bom_cache-warnings instead of raw elapsed time, since total plan elapsed time is now dominated by the separate, currently-degraded sap_valuation_client/sap_inventory_client calls rather than BOM cache performance - this is a test-expectation staleness issue, not a functional bug.
critical_code_review_comments: bom_cache_service.py: _apply_override extraction is clean and correctly shared between _fetch_live and _fetch_live_batch - no logic duplication or divergence found.

_fetch_live_batch's documented limitation (skips the SelectionByProductionBillOfMaterialID direct-ID-match _fetch_live tries first) is a reasonable, explicitly-documented tradeoff - verified it doesn't cause incorrect results, only a missed pre-warm opportunity for the rare literal-BOM-ID case, which falls through safely to the normal per-item path.

bulk_prefetch's use of a single Mongo $in query to skip already-cached ids before batching is efficient and correctly idempotent - verified via warm-run zero-bom_cache_service-warning log correlation.

purchasing_plan.py/mrp_service.py integration of bulk_prefetch is a minimal, surgical change (single extra call before existing loops) with no alteration to the existing resolution/fallback logic - reduces regression risk.

refresh_stale_nodes' coarser whole-chunk-fails-together degradation (vs old per-item) is consistent with the documented tradeoff from iteration_67 and does not lose data (untouched cache entries retried next 6h cycle) - confirmed via log inspection during this session's background refresh run.

ConnectTimeoutError' at the exact 18:20:02 timestamp inside the failing test's window).
